message.content:
The Declaration of Independence was signed by **56 delegates** from the thirteen colonies who had gathered at the Second Continental Congress in Philadelphia. The signers were:

| Signer | State | Notable Contributions |
|--------|-------|-----------------------|
| John Hancock | Massachusetts | President of the Continental Congress; his bold signature became a symbol of American patriotism. |
| Thomas Jefferson | Virginia | Principal author of the Declaration; later became the third U.S. President. |
| Benjamin Franklin | Pennsylvania | Renowned statesman, scientist, and diplomat; helped secure French support during the Revolution. |
| John Adams | Massachusetts | Future second U.S. President; key advocate for independence. |
| Samuel Adams | Massachusetts | Revolutionary leader and political activist. |
| George Washington | Virginia | Commander-in-Chief of the Continental Army; later the first U.S. President. |
| John Jay | New York | Diplomat and future first Chief Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court. |
| James Madison | Virginia | Future fourth U.S. President; key architect of the Constitution. |
| Alexander Hamilton | New York | Future first Secretary of Treasury; influential Founding Father. |
| Patrick Henry | Virginia | Famous orator (“Give me liberty, or give me death!”). |
| ... | ... | ... |

(For brevity, only a few are shown here; the full list includes representatives from each colony such as Robert Livingston, William Floyd, John Witherspoon, and many others.)

These men signed the document on **July 4, 1776** (though the formal signing ceremony actually took place on August 2, 1776). Their signatures marked the formal declaration of the thirteen colonies as independent states, ending British rule and laying the groundwork for the United States of America.
